We'll begin by considering the square matrix $$ A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp 0 \amp 2 \\ 2 \amp 2 \amp 1 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $$

Describe the solution space to the equation $A\xvec = \threevec343$ by augmenting $A$ and finding the reduced row echelon form.

Using [proposition-invertible-rref], explain why $A$ is invertible and find its inverse.

Now use the inverse to solve the equation $A\xvec = \threevec343$ and verify that your result agrees with what you found in part a.

If you have defined a matrix B in Sage, you can find it's inverse as B.inverse() or B^-1. Use Sage to find the inverse of the matrix $$ B = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -2 \amp -1 \\ -1 \amp 5 \amp 6 \\ 5 \amp -4 \amp 6 \\ \end{array}\right] $$ and use it to solve the equation $B\xvec = \threevec83{36}$.

If $A$ and $B$ are the two matrices defined in this activity, find their product $AB$ and verify that it is invertible.

Compute the products $A^{-1}B^{-1}$ and $B^{-1}A^{-1}$. Which one agrees with $(AB)^{-1}$?

Explain your finding by considering the product $$ (AB)(B^{-1}A^{-1}) $$ and using associativity to regroup the products so that the middle two terms are multiplied first.
